findings.mechanism: Ja'alna is the carrier; the paired bayn heads and hijab object specify a position, so the making predicate reads as relational placement.
findings.reader_payoff: The barrier is perceived as arranged between the parties.
findings.containment: The local syntax selects placement/configuration and does not require creation from nothing.

epistemic.reason: The object and spatial complement directly ground the placement branch and its bounded state-change facet.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: birini veya şeyi belirli bir duruma getirme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Var olan bir katılımcının durumunu, niteliğini veya konumunu değiştiren ettirici işlemi bildirir.
branch_activations.carrier: The first-person plural perfect ja'alna.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The repeated between heads and the barrier object specify a position for the thing made.
branch_activations.activation: The causative making predicate contacts a two-pole spatial complement, so its object is configured as a barrier between the parties.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The barrier is placed into a relation between the reciter and the defined group.
branch_activations.boundary: This is relational placement/configuration; it does not require creation from nothing.

findings.title: The conditional turns to divine action
findings.claim: After the addressed recitation protasis, first-person plural ja'alna begins the response and pivots the clause to divine action.
findings.mechanism: Qara'ta supplies the conditional act; ja'alna is the apodosis carrier, changing the grammatical actor as the barrier relation is asserted.
findings.reader_payoff: The answer arrives as an act, not a detached description.
findings.containment: The first-person plural form is stated from the supplied focus; no wider discourse shift is required.

epistemic.reason: The claim follows from the supplied focus surface and trusted aligned evidence.

findings.title: The interval both separates and relates
findings.claim: The paired bayn heads create one interval between two parties; the barrier divides them while their shared construction keeps them in relation.
findings.mechanism: The repeated locative head is the carrier; hijab and wa independently trigger the barrier and coordinated poles, bringing interval and relation branches into contact.
findings.reader_payoff: The interval is not an empty gap between unrelated worlds: it is a shared relation-space that divides.
findings.containment: The relation is grammatical/spatial; it does not imply intimacy, agreement, or a positive bond.

epistemic.reason: The locative heads, coordinator, and barrier are on the focus surface; the connecting relation remains bounded by separation.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek anlam iki veya daha çok taraf arasındaki orta, aralık ve iç konumdur.
branch_activations.carrier: The two bayn heads, one suffixed to the reciter and one governing the second group.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Ja'alna places a barrier as the object occupying the relation.
branch_activations.activation: The interval carrier meets the barrier object and supplies the boundary's relational location.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The barrier occupies a shared interval between the reciter and the defined group.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch concerns interval/position, not an act of separating by itself.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek anlam taraflar arasında bulunan bağ ve bağlantıdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The paired bayn interval heads.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The coordinating wa joins the two poles while hijab occupies their shared interval.
branch_activations.activation: The conjunction and barrier contact the relation branch: the same frame that separates the parties also keeps them in one grammatical relation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The barrier relation divides two parties without making them unrelated.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not claim intimacy, agreement, or a positive bond between the parties.

findings.title: The suffix anchors the first pole
findings.claim: Baynaka places the addressed reciter as the first pole inside the interval; the bare second bayn and its clause build the other side.
findings.mechanism: Bayn with its second-person suffix is the carrier; the repeated head and relative-clause group trigger the paired relation, making the reciter an anchored side of the barrier frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The reciter is grammatically inside the between-frame.
findings.containment: The suffix identifies a discourse participant and does not assert physical location.

epistemic.reason: The QAC suffix and parallel second head directly ground the two-pole interval.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek anlam iki veya daha çok taraf arasındaki orta, aralık ve iç konumdur.

findings.title: The connector binds the repeated cadence
findings.claim: The short wa between repeated bayn phrases binds their sound while keeping the two interval heads distinct.
findings.mechanism: The conjunction is the carrier; the repeated phrases on either side trigger its linking role, producing a linked cadence without merging their syntax.
findings.reader_payoff: The rhythm connects while preserving both sides.
findings.containment: This is a local cadence effect and makes no separate lexical claim for wa.

epistemic.reason: The claim follows from the supplied focus surface and trusted aligned evidence.

findings.title: Coordination preserves two poles
findings.claim: The middle wa coordinates two between-phrases, preserving a first pole and a second clause-defined pole.
findings.mechanism: Wa is the carrier; baynaka and the second bayn with its relative complement are the syntactic triggers, so coordination joins the poles without making the second group a modifier of the first.
findings.reader_payoff: Both sides of the barrier remain legible in the grammar.
findings.containment: This describes coordination and adds no separate referent.

epistemic.reason: The claim follows from the supplied focus surface and trusted aligned evidence.

findings.title: The following clause clarifies the second pole
findings.claim: The bare second bayn opens an interval pole that the relative clause makes identifiable by the group's continuing non-belief.
findings.mechanism: The second bayn is the carrier; the relative pronoun and negated-belief clause supply its complement, bringing clarification into contact with the locative construction.
findings.reader_payoff: The second side is defined by a stance rather than left as a bare location.
findings.containment: Bayn remains an interval head; this clarification is local, and the 36:9 comparison is excluded.

epistemic.reason: The focus relative clause grounds the clarification relation; the wider 36:9 comparison is excluded.

branch_activations.boundary: Bayn remains an interval head; clarification is supplied by its clause, not a new finite verb sense.

findings.title: Mirrored between-phrases enact separation
findings.claim: The repeated bayn heads assign each party its own pole, and the barrier in their interval gives that symmetry a separating effect.
findings.mechanism: The two between-phrases are the carrier; ja'alna and hijab trigger a placed obstruction, so the separation branch colors the repeated interval as distinct sides.
findings.reader_payoff: The interval is heard twice as a relation with a dividing center.
findings.containment: Bayn remains a locative interval; separation is an effect of the full construction, not a verb sense assigned to the adverb.

epistemic.reason: The repeated interval and explicit barrier independently ground the separation pressure.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek anlam ayrılma, kopma ve tarafların birbirinden ayrı hale gelmesidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The repeated between heads that build separate poles.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Ja'alna places hijab between the reciter and the group.

branch_activations.boundary: Bayn remains a locative interval, not a verb meaning to detach; separation is the effect of the full construction.

findings.title: The following clause builds the group's identity
findings.claim: Alladhina introduces a group whose identity is supplied by the negated-belief clause rather than by tribe or inherited label.
findings.mechanism: The relative pronoun is the carrier; la yu'minun supplies the defining property, changing a bare audience category into a behavior-defined class.
findings.reader_payoff: The second pole is defined by the group's stated belief stance.
findings.containment: This clause gives one defining property here; it does not deny that the group has other identities.

epistemic.reason: The claim follows from the supplied focus surface and trusted aligned evidence.

findings.title: The relative group fills the second pole
findings.claim: The relative pronoun is governed by the preceding bayn and embeds the clause-defined group as the interval's second pole.
findings.mechanism: Alladhina is the carrier; the second bayn is the governing trigger and the following clause completes the group, changing an open interval into specified participants.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees who occupies the other side of the relation.
findings.containment: The attachment does not reduce the group's identity to this clause for every purpose.

epistemic.reason: The claim follows from the supplied focus surface and trusted aligned evidence.

findings.title: Recitation occasions an unseen boundary
findings.claim: The ordinary reading begins with hearers failing to receive the recitation; the conditional and response also configure an unseen access boundary around each recitation event.
findings.mechanism: Qara'ta with al-Qur'an supplies the event; idha makes it conditional; ja'alna effects the barrier; paired bayn locates it between two parties; hijab blocks access; masturan predicates hiddenness of the barrier. Together these contacts change unmarked non-reception into a placed, relational obstacle whose operation is unseen.
findings.reader_payoff: Non-reception becomes perceptible as a relation formed around recitation, with the barrier that blocks access itself hidden.
findings.containment: The trace is legacy-attributed. It does not claim every recitation is blocked, identify a hidden agent or motive, or turn unresolved qara into a verified lexical gloss.

epistemic.reason: All focus coordinates and roots agree with the supplied QAC surface, but the integrated roles come from legacy_unbound HFT and remain attributed.

findings.title: A refused future horizon becomes present distance
findings.claim: The group label is retained, while refusal of belief in the Hereafter can also be read as a future horizon that organizes present distance between the parties.
findings.mechanism: The negated belief verb supplies withheld assent; al-akhirah is its future-oriented object; paired bayn converts that temporal refusal into present distance; hijab gives the distance an access-blocking effect. The four attributed roles change an audience label into a present gap oriented toward what comes after.
findings.reader_payoff: The Hereafter remains the local object of belief, while refusal of that horizon is also rendered as present distance.
findings.containment: Al-akhirah remains the ordinary Hereafter noun; no delay verb, measurable distance, or claim of physical/social/salvation exclusion is added. HFT roles remain attributed, and only registered branches receive copied glosses and facets.

epistemic.reason: Word indices and roots match the focus surface exactly, but the before/after integration is a legacy_unbound HFT interpretation.
